subject: BrightLayer: Executive sponsor recap — outcomes, risks, procurement path
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Seth Coleman <seth.coleman@brightlayer.com>, Laura Ng <laura.ng@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + next steps from today’s exec discovery

Thanks again for a productive call today. Short recap for the executive team and next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- Production latency spikes during batch uploads (api 99th percentile ~450ms during peak) causing timeouts on your clinical ingestion pipeline.
- Cost unpredictability when usage scales across inference-heavy workflows; current infra lacks consistent per-token economics across nightly batches.
- Regulatory/data concerns: PHI in prompts and need for strict retention controls + audit logs.

Business outcomes BrightLayer shared:
- Reduce per-request inference cost by ~35–45% for inference-heavy endpoints.
- 99th percentile token latency below ~200ms for standard 2k token sequences during business hours.
- Maintain SOC 2-equivalent controls for auditability and a documented data residency policy.

Procurement path we sketched:
- 90-day pilot (reserved small cluster + SLOs for latency) scoped by SOW.
- Procurement to review SOW and issue PO to Redwood; target pilot start ~June 7 if PO in place by May 31.
- Post-pilot: annual reserved capacity (committed monthly bill) with optional burst.

Risks / open questions we flagged:
- Data retention and deletion windows (are 90-day windows acceptable for BrightLayer legal?)
- Model output safety / hallucination mitigation for clinical content — need guardrails and eval pass/fail criteria.
- SSO & identity — we proposed SAML for admin access and a service account key for programmatic calls.

Immediate asks for BrightLayer:
1) Confirm procurement contact and PO timing.
2) Confirm whether 90-day retention is OK or whether you need shorter window (30 days).
3) Share the security questionnaire (if you prefer we fill your form or share our SOC2 artifact).

Attachments: pilot-scope-v1.pdf (draft SOW / pilot scope)

If that captures it, I’ll: 1) loop in Laura Bennett (CS) to draft pilot success criteria and runbook, 2) have Marissa pull SOC2/INFRA artifacts and 3) get a DocuSign SOW ready for your procurement once you confirm contacts.

Thanks — Logan
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
log@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Seth Coleman <seth.coleman@brightlayer.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Ng <laura.ng@brightlayer.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps from today’s exec discovery

Thanks Logan — this is helpful and aligns with what we need. A few quick notes:  

- Procurement contact: Monica Ruiz (cc’d on this thread) will own contracting and PO timing.
- Tentative timeline: procurement aims to review SOW this week; we can likely issue PO by 5/28 if SOW is stable.
- Data retention: Legal is inclined toward 60–90 days; they asked us to flag any platform limitations on shorter windows.

I attached a short security checklist we use internally (BrightLayer_security_questions.pdf). Laura and I will review the pilot-scope and circle back with any major asks.

Appreciate you capturing the success metrics — we want to see the latency/cost baselines and proposed SLOs in the SOW. Otherwise, please proceed to loop in CS/legal as needed.

Best,
Seth
Seth Coleman
Head of Platform Engineering, BrightLayer
seth.coleman@brightlayer.com | +1 (646) 555-6082

Looping internal ops and GTM owners — Seth confirmed procurement lead (Monica) and attached their security checklist. Below are the internal action items I recommend before we send a finalized SOW: 

1) Security artifacts: Upload SOC2 report + system architecture diagram to secure drive and prepare a one-page data residency note. Owner: Ben (due 5/24).
2) Pilot success criteria / runbook: Laura to define SLOs, evaluation prompts, and rollback criteria. Owner: Laura (due 5/26).
3) SOW redlines: I’ll prepare the SOW with optional 60-day retention redline and an explicit clause for model output monitoring. Owner: Marissa (draft 5/21).
4) Commercial: Logan to capture baseline cost numbers and expected committed capacity for pilot (estimate 4 GPU nodes / 2–3 requests/sec average).
5) DocuSign readiness: Legal to prep standard Redwood terms; once Monica confirms PO timing we’ll push SOW via DocuSign.

Attachments: internal-ask-list.txt

> Procurement contact: Monica Ruiz (cc’d on this thread) will own contracting and PO timing.

Ben / Laura — please confirm owners and whether we need an NDA before sharing SOC2 artifacts.

Subject: Re: BrightLayer SOW / procurement next steps

Thanks all — procurement here. We reviewed the draft scope and are ready to proceed with a 90-day pilot. A few notes from procurement/legal: 

- Please route the finalized SOW to procurement@brightlayer.com. We require a DocuSign envelope for signature (link provided below once SOW is final).
- We request a modification to the data retention clause: prefer 60 days rather than 90. If Redwood can support 60 days, procurement will clear the PO faster.
- Please include a one-page statement of data handling (how PHI is isolated, deletion workflow, and audit log retention).

DocuSign placeholder: https://docusign.com/sandbox/0b3a9f
Procurement contact card attached: procurement_contact.vcf

We aim to approve and release PO by 5/28 if the SOW reflects the 60-day retention change. Once we receive DocuSign I’ll confirm the approvers.

Regards,
Monica Ruiz
Procurement Manager, BrightLayer
